surfaceForm: An indicative envelope, for an R1 institution, would be on the order of two to four engineers shared with the platform-engineering function.
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch14-orchestration-EN.tex :: \section{Reference instantiation: Argo Workflows + Crossplane + GitOps} (\paragraph{Operational considerations.})
proposedGenericDecision: Express staffing as a role-based, size-relative band tied to a generic institutional-tier descriptor rather than the US-Carnegie 'R1' classification, which is jurisdiction/system-bound and does not map onto every higher-education system.
suggestedLocalizationVariable: \InstitutionTier (e.g. 'a research-intensive institution') and \OrchestrationFteBand (e.g. 'two to four engineers')
rationale: 'R1 institution' is a Carnegie Classification term specific to the US system; a generic Reference should describe institutional scale in system-neutral terms. The FTE figure is also a sizing assumption that should be a localization variable, though the band itself is generic guidance not a UL-specific number.

surfaceForm: The phase-2 international university network anticipated by this Reference would be one of the contexts in which a shared library of academic orchestration compositions might emerge.
proposedGenericDecision: Decouple from a specific 'phase-2 international university network' programme of the originating institution; reframe as a generic future-collaboration context (a multi-institution consortium adopting this Reference).
rationale: 'The phase-2 international university network anticipated by this Reference' implies a concrete roadmap/programme belonging to the source institution's deployment plan, an implicit self-reference that is not institution-agnostic. Should be generalized to 'a multi-institution consortium adopting this architecture'.

surfaceForm: It contributes to \gls{gdpr}~Art.~25 ... and to NIS2~Art.~21(2)(c) ... business continuity through declarative redeployability ...
proposedGenericDecision: Regulatory anchors here are EU-level instruments (GDPR, NIS2) cited at the directive/regulation article level, which is acceptably generic for any EU-based adopter; however NIS2 is a Directive requiring national transposition, so the framing implicitly assumes an EU member-state adopter without naming the transposing jurisdiction. Add a transposition caveat or parameterize the jurisdiction.
suggestedLocalizationVariable: \NationalTransposition (optional note pointing to the local NIS2 transposition law)
rationale: GDPR/NIS2/ISO/NIST/COBIT citations are framework-level and broadly portable, so 'keep' is the primary recommendation. The only implicit specificity is the unstated EU-member-state assumption behind NIS2 (a Directive transposed nationally); this is a soft flag rather than a UL-specific leak.
